note: A retirement is a preservation claim, not a story about a red run. Every entry registers the retired path (file), the original path it was retired from (original_path), the sha256 of the preserved bytes (sha256), a free-text reason, the registration date (retired_on) and the review that accepted the retirement (review_reference). scripts/verify-retirement-registry.js reads no test output. It checks four things from files and hashes: (a) preserved - the file at the registered path hashes to the registered sha256; (b) complete - every file under tests/legacy/ is registered, including the session harness the retired pd275 suites require; (c) not a fake retirement - the original path does not still carry the registered bytes; (d) re-evaluable - the registered bytes are put back at the original path and run, and a passing run is named as a receipt (KDNA-RETIREMENT-RESTORABLE) because the entry is not stale. Only (a)-(c) decide the exit code.
